title: HR Diagram
body:
The **Hertzsprung-Russell diagram** plots stars by temperature against luminosity, and it is
the organising figure of stellar astronomy. Temperature runs backwards along the horizontal
axis by convention, hot on the left, and luminosity spans a factor of a billion so the vertical
axis is logarithmic.

```
luminosity
   10⁴ |    supergiants
       |
   10² |         red giants
       |   \
   10⁰ |     \  main sequence (the Sun sits here)
       |       \
  10⁻² |  white   \
       |  dwarfs    \
       +------------------------------
        30,000 K        3,000 K
```

Stars fall into a few regions and leave most of the plot empty, and that clustering is the
result worth explaining. About 90% lie on the main sequence, the diagonal band, and a star's
position along it is determined almost entirely by its mass. The mass-luminosity relation makes
luminosity rise roughly as the fourth power of mass, so a star ten times the Sun's mass is
thousands of times more luminous and burns through its fuel in a few million years while the
Sun lasts ten billion.

The off-sequence regions mark stages of stellar death, so one star occupies different regions
at different points in its life. The [[Red Giant]] branch is where a star goes after its
core hydrogen runs out, and the [[White Dwarf]] region holds what is left when the outer
layers depart. A star therefore traces a path across this diagram over its lifetime, which is
what turns a scatter plot into a life cycle.
